chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
His father (peace be upon him) said: Any man who mixes one part of the Quran with another has disbelieved.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to mix one part of the Quran with another in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from his father, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, that mixing one part of the Quran with another constitutes disbelief (kafara). This statement is interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the distortion (tahrif) of the text or the mixing of divine revelation with human words, emphasizing the preservation of the Quran's integrity as a condition of faith. The severity of the ruling underscores the Quran's status as the unaltered word of God, central to Shia theological identity.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his ancestors
that one who mixes one part of the Holy Quran with another, is a disbeliever.
